questions.question: A platform team needs mutual TLS between microservices, fine-grained traffic splitting, and telemetry - all injected via Envoy sidecar proxies with no application code changes. Which service mesh do they deploy?
questions.explanation: Istio implements the sidecar data plane (Envoy proxies) plus a control plane for mTLS, routing, and observability without touching app code.

questions.question: A release routes 5% of traffic to the new version, evaluates metrics, then widens to 25%, 50%, 100%, while feature flags gate the riskiest code paths throughout. Which umbrella term names this gradual, metrics-gated rollout style?
questions.explanation: Progressive delivery is the umbrella over canary releases, blue-green, and feature flags that de-risk rollout incrementally.

questions.question: A new checkout flow misbehaves at 2 a.m.; an operator disables it from a dashboard in seconds while the same deployed build keeps serving the old flow. Which mechanism made the instant rollback possible?
questions.explanation: A feature toggle wraps the new code in a runtime switch, so rollback needs no redeploy - the flag just turns off.

questions.question: A request times out after crossing six microservices; engineers attach one correlation ID at the gateway and later view a single timeline of every hop's latency. Which observability practice produced that timeline?
questions.explanation: Distributed tracing propagates a trace/span context across services so one request's path and latencies can be reassembled end to end.

questions.question: A company wants its images to run identically on Docker, containerd, and CRI-O with no vendor lock-in. Which industry specification defines the image and runtime formats that make this portability possible?
questions.explanation: OCI standardizes the image format, runtime spec, and distribution spec, so conformant runtimes can run the same images.

questions.question: The same container image runs in dev, staging, and prod; only API endpoints and log levels differ per environment. Which Kubernetes object should carry those non-sensitive values?
questions.explanation: ConfigMaps decouple non-sensitive per-environment settings from the image; sensitive values would belong in Secrets instead.

questions.question: A web API saturates at 80% CPU every noon; the team wants Kubernetes to add pod replicas automatically whenever CPU exceeds 70% and scale back at night. Which controller does this?
questions.explanation: The HPA watches metrics such as CPU and adjusts the replica count horizontally - unlike the VPA, which resizes pod requests.

questions.question: All cluster manifests live in Git; a controller watches the repo and continuously converges the live cluster to match, and the team manages each deployment through an 'Application' custom resource in its web UI. Which GitOps tool is this?
questions.explanation: ArgoCD is the declarative GitOps controller for Kubernetes whose 'Application' CRD syncs a repo path into a namespace and reports drift.

questions.question: Following the twelve-factor methodology, a team builds one artifact once and promotes it through dev, staging, and prod, injecting environment-specific settings only at runtime. Which principle are they applying?
questions.explanation: Externalized configuration keeps env-specific settings outside the build artifact so the identical image or binary can run in every environment.

questions.question: In one quarter a team made 40 production deployments, and 6 of them caused degraded service that needed a hotfix or rollback. Compute the Change Failure Rate.
questions.explanation: Change Failure Rate = failed changes / total changes = 6 / 40 = 0.15 = 15%.

questions.question: A set of Pods needs a stable DNS name and load-balanced access inside the cluster. Which Kubernetes object provides this?
questions.explanation: A Kubernetes Service exposes a logical set of Pods with a stable IP/DNS name and load balancing across them.

questions.question: Database passwords must be encrypted, stored in version control safely, and injected only at deploy time. Which DevOps practice covers this?
questions.explanation: Secrets management stores credentials encrypted (e.g., Vault, SOPS, sealed-secrets) and injects them at runtime or deploy time.

questions.question: A downstream service keeps timing out and calls pile up, exhausting resources. Which resilience pattern makes the client fail fast and stop calling it?
questions.explanation: The Circuit Breaker pattern trips after repeated failures, failing fast to prevent cascading errors and allow recovery.

questions.question: Before full promotion, metrics from a small canary release are automatically evaluated against thresholds. Which deployment practice is this?
questions.explanation: Automated Canary Analysis statistically compares canary metrics to baselines before deciding to promote or roll back.

questions.question: A team randomly terminates production instances to verify the system survives failures. Which practice are they using?
questions.explanation: Chaos engineering deliberately injects failures (e.g., Netflix's Chaos Monkey) to prove and improve system resilience.

questions.question: A Kubernetes rolling update must keep at most one pod unavailable while creating at most one extra pod. The two RollingUpdate strategy fields that control this.
questions.explanation: rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable caps how many pods may be down; maxSurge caps how many extra pods may be created above desired count.

questions.question: An SLO promises 99.9% availability over a 30-day month. The maximum allowed downtime (error budget) in minutes.
questions.explanation: 30 days x 24 h x 60 min = 43,200 minutes; 0.1% of that (99.9% SLO) = 43.2 minutes of allowed downtime.

questions.question: A pipeline builds, tests, and deploys to staging automatically, but the production release still requires a human approval click. This describes which practice, as opposed to continuous deployment?
alternatives: CD with a manual approval step
questions.explanation: Continuous Delivery keeps every change deployable but leaves production release a business decision; continuous deployment removes that manual gate entirely.

questions.question: Two engineers run 'terraform apply' at the same time against a locally stored state file and corrupt it. The backend feature/practice that prevents concurrent state modification.
questions.answer: Remote state backend with state locking
alternatives: Remote backend with locking (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB)
questions.explanation: Storing state in a remote backend that supports locking (such as S3 with a lock table) serializes applies so only one can modify state at a time.

questions.question: Last month a team had four production incidents that took 20, 40, 45, and 55 minutes respectively to fully restore. What is their mean time to restore service?
questions.explanation: Mean time to restore = (20 + 40 + 45 + 55) / 4 = 160 / 4 = 40 minutes - DORA's stability metric for recovery speed.
